threads.body: [General] SOFA extracts codes only from failures, so emitting them as `rpc.status_code` duplicates `error.type` on spans and duration metrics, contrary to `.github/instructions/emitted-telemetry.instructions.md:37–39`. It also exposes the synthetic `SERVER_UNDECLARED_ERROR` from `TracingFilter.extractException()` as a captured status when the response provides only an error flag/message. Keep numeric extraction in `getErrorType()`, leave SOFA's status getter at its null default, and adjust the SOFA getter, span, and metric assertions accordingly.

Fixed the synthetic fallback case in cd4fb137b3d086e3e9b25f501b6a1358cc921ff4. Synchronous and asynchronous completion now distinguish the instrumentation-created exception, omit its `rpc.status_code`, and preserve its existing `error.type`. Genuine SOFA codes, including the same numeric code, remain eligible; the added regression coverage checks both cases on spans and metrics.

The duplication itself is intentional. This change reverses the repository-specific omission policy at the user's request, and #20954 removes that exception separately.

@copilot Update this PR directly with one focused correction to SOFA RPC status provenance.

Keep the requested rpc.status_code emission for genuine SOFA framework/server/client codes, even when it duplicates error.type. The review's objection based on the old failure-only omission policy is intentionally not applicable: the user explicitly requested reversing that policy, with its documentation removal in a separate PR. Do not remove SOFA status support or restore that omission policy.

The review does identify a real fallback-provenance issue. TracingFilter.extractException() creates a new SofaRpcException(SERVER_UNDECLARED_ERROR, errorMsg) when a response exposes only an error flag/message. That code is fabricated by our instrumentation, not obtained from SOFA's response or an actual supplied RPC exception. The new getter currently exposes it as rpc.status_code because getErrorType() delegates to getRpcStatusCode(). Preserve the existing error.type classification and exception behavior, but do not emit a status for this instrumentation-created fallback.

Distinguish that synthesized fallback from actual SofaRpcException codes on every relevant synchronous and asynchronous path. A genuine SERVER_UNDECLARED_ERROR code supplied by the framework must still be eligible, so do not simply blacklist its numeric value or discard all response failures. Keep exception-only and unavailable statuses omitted. Preserve Thrift behavior, legacy mode, preview/dup selection, gRPC's existing emission, and existing span and metric error classification.

Add focused regression coverage for error-flag/error-message-only responses and their synthetic fallback, including synchronous/asynchronous behavior where applicable, and for genuine supplied codes including the same numeric code. Adjust affected span/metric expectations to omit only fabricated statuses, not real codes. Apply the relevant formatter and run focused tests. Evidence is Copilot review 5640556097, root comment 4368902649, and the current TracingFilter.extractException() implementation.

Keep this correction within this PR's RPC scope. Do not edit docs/instrumentation-list.yaml, database code, generated changelog entries, or .github/instructions/emitted-telemetry.instructions.md. Those generated/policy files are intentionally excluded or handled separately.

@copilot Fix the latest-dependency CI failure on this PR directly with the smallest appropriate SOFA RPC test-fixture correction.

The user asked to address the CI failure in PR #20952, then explicitly requested cloud execution once the cause was identified. The deterministic fix-ci bundle was downloaded with .github/scripts/pr-triage/fix_ci.py 20952 --download-only. Its summary identifies one failed non-aggregate job, build / test-latest-deps / testLatestDeps1, job 121036114925, at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/actions/runs/40143744750/job/121036114925. CI runs Gradle with -PtestLatestDeps=true.

The downloaded log identifies the root cause before any telemetry assertions: SofaRpcTest.suppliedStatusCodeIsEmitted(boolean) and syntheticFallbackStatusIsOmitted(boolean), each for async=false and async=true, fail in SofaRpcTest.assertStatusCode at FilterInvoker construction. The stack is SofaRpcRuntimeException: Can't access copy proxyClass, through BeanUtils.copyPropertiesToMap, AbstractInterfaceConfig.getConfigValueCache, FilterInvoker.<init>, caused by ConsumerConfig.getProxyClass reporting "The value of config consumer.interface [null] is illegal, interfaceId must be not null". The repeated attempts fail identically; this is not an infrastructure or flaky assertion failure.

In instrumentation/sofa-rpc-5.4/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/sofarpc/v5_4/SofaRpcTest.java, assertStatusCode currently creates ConsumerConfig<?> config = new ConsumerConfig<>().setInJVM(false), with no interfaceId. Its request also uses the fictitious service name "test.Service". Make this fixture valid for the supported baseline SOFA 5.4.0 and latest dependency versions, using a real loadable test-service interface and coherent request/configuration fields as appropriate. Existing setup in instrumentation/sofa-rpc-5.4/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/sofarpc/v5_4/AbstractSofaRpcTest.java configures real HelloService/ErrorService interfaces with setInterfaceId; reuse the relevant existing pattern rather than adding production workarounds or unnecessary abstractions.

Preserve the substantive regression coverage and intended production behavior. Both synchronous and asynchronous tests must still distinguish an instrumentation-manufactured SERVER_UNDECLARED_ERROR from a genuinely supplied exception with that same code, 199. Keep the existing error.type behavior and span/metric assertions, omit only fabricated rpc.status_code, preserve actual supplied status emission in preview/dup, and preserve legacy mode. Do not skip, disable, remove, weaken, or broadly mock away these tests to make CI pass. Keep Thrift and other integrations unchanged.

Apply the narrow module formatter directly before focused validation. Reproduce and validate the relevant SOFA library suite with -PtestLatestDeps=true, and verify baseline compatibility as well, including the configured semconv variants where relevant. The narrow test target is :instrumentation:sofa-rpc-5.4:library:test, with the failure rooted in SofaRpcTest. Do not run clean, disable the cache, or force all tasks to rerun. Report the exact focused commands and results in your coding-session evidence.

Keep this fix scoped to the identified CI failure on the existing PR. Do not edit docs/instrumentation-list.yaml, database code, generated changelog entries, or .github/instructions/emitted-telemetry.instructions.md. The old omission exception is intentionally removed by a separate PR and must not be restored.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly with the agreed RPC getter-ownership cleanup. Do not create another PR.

The user reviewed the status-to-error-classifier dependency and approved this behavior-preserving plan. A status getter must not depend on getErrorType(), because status extraction and error classification have different responsibilities. In SofaRpcAttributesGetter, getRpcStatusCode() currently checks TracingFilter.isSyntheticFallbackError() and then returns getErrorType(request, response, error).

Extract a small neutral helper in SofaRpcAttributesGetter that reads and validates the numeric SofaRpcException code. Have getErrorType() consume that raw code, and have getRpcStatusCode() consume it subject to the existing synthetic-provenance exclusion. Do not mechanically reverse the delegation: routing error.type through the filtered status getter would lose the existing classification of instrumentation-created fallback exceptions. Do not introduce a shared extraction framework or redesign the shared RPC API.

Preserve all existing telemetry behavior: supported SOFA code categories and bounds, exception-class fallback, unavailable success statuses, and preview/duplicate-semconv gating with the exact key rpc.status_code. The user intentionally requested emitting real statuses even when equal to error.type. Do not restore the old omission exception or rename the key to rpc.response.status_code.

Preserve the prior provenance correction on every synchronous and asynchronous path. A genuine supplied SERVER_UNDECLARED_ERROR code 199 remains a captured status; the instrumentation-created fallback with the same code must have no status while retaining its error.type. Keep TracingFilter's scoped state restoration intact. Preserve the latest CI fixture correction in bf9e664ac895ba5f707e7a78528048adb944b004: SofaRpcTest uses the real ErrorService interface, real method names, and matching ConsumerConfig.interfaceId.

Thrift already extracts application-reply statuses independently from transport error classifications and _OTHER. Leave it unchanged, along with gRPC, the shared attribute extractors, database code, the separate policy-removal PR, docs/instrumentation-list.yaml, and generated changelog entries.

Keep the existing getter, span, and metric regressions. Add or adjust focused coverage only if the refactor exposes a real gap, particularly genuine versus synthesized code 199 and status/error classification divergence. Do not weaken assertions or disable tests. Apply the narrow module formatter directly before focused validation, verify baseline and latest supported SOFA dependencies and relevant existing semconv variants, and report exact commands and outcomes in the coding-session evidence. Do not run clean, bypass the build cache, or force unchanged tasks to rerun.

Replace TracingFilter's SYNTHETIC_FALLBACK_ERROR ThreadLocal with per-call state on the existing instrumentation-owned SofaRpcRequest wrapper, which is already carried through asynchronous completion. Pass that wrapper into extractException and mark it only when our instrumentation manufactures the fallback SofaRpcException. Restore extractException's nullable Throwable return, remove ExtractedException and the end wrapper, and call instrumenter.end directly. Ensure both synchronous and asynchronous paths, supplied exceptions, thrown exceptions, and nested calls preserve the intended per-call provenance without ambient thread state. Keep the state package-private and avoid unnecessary public API additions.

My subsequent suggestion to delegate the status getter to getErrorType was mistaken and is NOT part of this assignment. Have getRpcStatusCode consult the request's provenance flag and independently consume the neutral helper; getErrorType must continue classifying synthetic fallback errors normally.

Combine SofaRpcTest.syntheticFallbackStatusIsOmitted and suppliedStatusCodeIsEmitted and their forwarding helper into one parameterized test with all four async/syntheticFallback combinations, for example using CsvSource. Preserve the real ErrorService interface, coherent request methods and ConsumerConfig.interfaceId fixture correction. Do not weaken span or metric assertions or remove coverage.

This is behavior-preserving simplification. Genuine supplied SOFA codes, including SERVER_UNDECLARED_ERROR code 199, must still emit rpc.status_code in preview/dup even when equal to error.type. Instrumentation-created fallback errors with that same code must omit only rpc.status_code while retaining existing error.type and exception behavior. Preserve supported numeric bounds, unavailable success statuses, legacy mode, and asynchronous behavior. Leave the shared RPC API, Thrift, gRPC, policy-removal work, generated files, and unrelated code unchanged.

Apply the narrow module formatter immediately before focused validation.
